## What's New overhaul: releases, highlights, targeting, preview (2026-10-06, branch feature/whats-new-overhaul)

Customer release notes moved from "one Markdown blob in a blocking popup" to releases made of highlight cards, with a topbar entry point, a real changelog, per-customer read state, targeting, scheduling and an admin preview.

**What was weak before.** Create-only admin form (no editing), publish was instant with no schedule and no confirmation, the admin preview was a hand-kept copy of the popup markup (it had already drifted from the feed), the changelog page ignored service targeting (customers saw updates for products they don't have) while the popup applied it, a new signup was greeted by the whole back-catalogue one modal at a time, there was no "remind me later", no "Try it" link, and the popup's hard-coded slate/white classes ignored the portal tokens. `components/customer/WhatsNew.tsx` was dead code.

**Model (additive, `prisma/manual-migration-whats-new-overhaul.sql`, idempotent, verified to leave `prisma migrate diff` empty against the new schema).** `UpdateAnnouncement` gains `summary`, `highlights` (Json: `WnHighlight[]`), `categories` (derived on save), `heroImageUrl`, `scheduledFor`, `audience` (ALL | GAME | VPS), `regions` (node region keys), `emailAnnounce` (default false), `emailStartedAt/FinishedAt`, `createdBy/publishedBy`. `status` is now DRAFT | SCHEDULED | PUBLISHED. `UserAnnouncementSeen` gains `state` (READ default = what every existing row meant, or SNOOZED) and `snoozedUntil`. New `UpdateAnnouncementDelivery` (unique per release+user) for the email.

**Rules — `lib/whats-new/core.ts` (pure, unit tested).**
- Categories: Game servers, VPS, Billing, Dashboard, Support, Performance & reliability. Legacy rows map from `serviceTypes`.
- Highlight validation: title + 1–2 line description + category required; "Try it" links must be in-app paths (no scheme, no `//`, no quotes/whitespace); images must live under `/whats-new/`, `/uploads/announcements/` or `/nx/` and need alt text.
- `effectiveStatus`: a SCHEDULED release is PUBLISHED once `scheduledFor` passes — checked at read time, no cron needed for visibility.
- `publishBlockers`: publish/schedule are REFUSED while any highlight is `availability: NEXT_UPDATE` ("ships with the next update"). `availability` is owner-only and is stripped from every customer payload.
- `isVisibleTo`: audience GAME/VPS needs a live server of that kind (servers in DELETING don't count); `regions` must intersect the customer's server regions; legacy `serviceTypes` still scope ALL-audience rows.
- `readState`: READ / SNOOZED (until `snoozedUntil`, then UNREAD again) / UNREAD; a release that went live before the account was created counts as READ.
- `inboxSummary`: the unread dot counts UNREAD + SNOOZED; the dialog auto-opens only for the newest release and only if it is UNREAD.

**Data layer — `lib/whats-new/data.ts`** (plain module, explicit ids, used by actions, preview route, worker and tests): `listVisibleReleases`, `inboxFor`, `markRead` (only ids the customer can see; forged/draft ids ignored), `snooze` (never downgrades READ), `saveRelease`, `publishRelease`, `scheduleRelease`, `unpublishRelease`, `markAllLive`, `emailSweep`. Server actions in `lib/actions-announcements.ts`; customer read-state writes are skipped while an admin impersonates, and the dialog never auto-opens over impersonation.

**Customer UI.**
- `components/nx/whatsnew/WhatsNewLauncher.tsx` — sparkles button in the topbar (mounted by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, next to the bell) with a cyan unread dot; opens the latest release; auto-opens the newest unread one once (not on /dashboard/whats-new). Replaces `components/customer/AnnouncementPopup.tsx` (removed from `app/dashboard/layout.tsx`).
- `components/nx/whatsnew/WhatsNewModal.tsx` — centred dialog on desktop, full-height sheet on phones (safe-area padded); aria-modal, labelled by the title, focus moves in, Tab trapped, Esc/X/backdrop/"Got it" = read, "Remind me later" = snooze for 24 h, "See all updates" link. Entrance animation via `motion-safe:animate-wn-rise/wn-fade` (keyframes in `app/globals.css`), so reduced motion gets a still dialog.
- `components/nx/whatsnew/ReleaseParts.tsx` — the ONE set of markup (highlight card with 16:9 image on a dark island so screenshots read the same in both themes, category chip, "Try it" link, hero) used by the dialog, the changelog and the admin editor's live preview.
- `components/nx/WhatsNewView.tsx` + `app/dashboard/whats-new/page.tsx` — changelog grouped by day, category filter chips (a filtered release shows only matching highlights), search, "Mark all read", a release counts as read after 1.5 s in view. Only releases the customer is targeted by.

**Admin.** `/admin/announcements` (`components/admin/AnnouncementsAdmin.tsx`): create + edit, highlight rows (reorder/remove, category, live vs next update, image + alt, Try-it link + label), audience + optional regions, header image, optional legacy Markdown notes, email toggle (default OFF, explained), side-by-side live preview with the real components, then per-row Edit / Preview ↗ / Mark all live / Publish now (confirm, names the email if on) / Schedule (datetime) / Unpublish or Cancel schedule / Delete, plus read and emailed counts. **Admin preview URL:** `/dashboard/whats-new/preview/<id>` (gated by `requireArea("platform")`, writes no read state, `?dialog=0` starts with the dialog closed) renders the release inside the real customer dashboard with the dialog open and the owner-only Live / Ships-with-next-update badges.

**Announcement email (opt-in).** Worker sweep `whats-new-email` every 5 min (`worker/whats-new-email.ts` → `emailSweep`): only releases with `emailAnnounce` that are live and unfinished; recipients are verified, non-suspended CUSTOMER accounts the release targets; a delivery row is claimed before each send (so overlap/crash never double-mails); 200 sends per sweep; `kind: "product_news"` so the customer's product-news preference is honoured inside `sendMail`, with a one-click unsubscribe header. Once sending has started the toggle can no longer be changed.

**Release files.** Releases can be authored as JSON (`prisma/whats-new/<slug>.json`) and loaded as a DRAFT with `npx tsx prisma/seed-whats-new.ts prisma/whats-new/<slug>.json` — always DRAFT, email forced off, idempotent by title, never touches a published release, refuses the production database unless `--allow-prod`. Images live in `public/whats-new/<slug>/` (WebP, 1280×720 framed product shots; no customer data).

**First draft: `prisma/whats-new/2026-10-release.json`** ("Easier mods, folder downloads and a faster live chat", 7 highlights; 2 live now — Minecraft newest-version default, Bedrock port fix; 5 ship with the next update — live chat, file/folder downloads, Mods tab, no player caps, dashboard server directory). Excluded on the owner's instruction: invoices, status notices, custom offers, the theme animation. Publishing it is refused until the five are deployed and marked live.

**Owner flow after deploy.** Apply the migration SQL (or `prisma db push`), deploy, then `npx tsx prisma/seed-whats-new.ts prisma/whats-new/2026-10-release.json --allow-prod`, open `/dashboard/whats-new/preview/<id>`, check it, "Mark all live" once the five branches are live, then Publish now or Schedule.

**Tests.** `test/whats-new.test.ts` (pure rules + the draft file: valid, DRAFT, email off, every image exists, no banned words such as provider/OVH/invoice/admin, publish refused). `test/whats-new-db.test.ts` (opt-in, throwaway DB: `WHATSNEW_TEST_DATABASE_URL` = `DATABASE_URL` on 127.0.0.1 non-5432 `/whatsnew`): drafts/schedules invisible, publish gate, audience + region targeting on real Server/Node rows, read/snooze/expiry, forged ids, pre-signup releases, payload without availability, email exactly once to the right people.
EOF

# What's New — DRAFT release (unpublished)

Source of truth: `prisma/whats-new/2026-10-release.json` on branch `feature/whats-new-overhaul`.
Status: **DRAFT**. Announcement email: **OFF**. Audience: all customers (no region limit).
Owner-only marks: **[LIVE]** = already on the live site; **[NEXT UPDATE]** = ships with the next deploy.
Publishing is refused by the app until every item is marked live.

Excluded on the owner's instruction: the new invoices (logo / specs / renewal price), status notices,
custom / one-click offers, and the light/dark theme animation. Also excluded as internal: OVH controls,
CPU reservations, reports, AI bot internals, SEO, the unpublished dedicated catalogue.

---

**WHAT'S NEW**

## Easier mods, folder downloads and a faster live chat

Seven improvements for game server owners: quicker Minecraft setup, a rebuilt Mods tab, downloads from
the Files tab, no player caps from us, a server directory in your dashboard, and a live chat that keeps
up with you.

Header image: `public/whats-new/2026-10-release/header.webp`

### 1. Minecraft starts on the newest version — Game servers — [LIVE]
When you deploy a Vanilla, Paper or Purpur server, the newest Minecraft release is now picked for you, so
your server matches what your players run. You can still choose any other version.
*Try it:* Deploy Minecraft → `/dashboard/deploy?product=game&family=minecraft`
*Image:* `minecraft-latest.webp` (deploy wizard, newest release preselected)

### 2. Bedrock servers ready to join on the latest version — Performance & reliability — [LIVE]
Fixed: a new Bedrock server on the newest version could start without opening its game port. New Bedrock
servers now run a build we have tested and open their port straight away.
*Try it:* Deploy Bedrock → `/dashboard/deploy?product=game&family=bedrock`
*Image:* `bedrock-port.webp` (branded illustration, no UI)

### 3. Live chat that keeps up with you — Support — [NEXT UPDATE] (feature/livechat-overhaul)
Messages arrive the moment they are sent. You can see when our team is typing and when your message has
been seen, paste or drag in screenshots, and chat full screen on your phone.
*Try it:* Open live chat → `/dashboard/support?tab=chat`
*Image:* `live-chat.webp` (mobile chat, Team online + Seen; placeholder names only)

### 4. Download files and whole folders — Game servers — [NEXT UPDATE] (feature/files-download)
Download any file from the Files tab, or tick several files and folders and get them as one .tar.gz
archive. Handy for keeping a copy of your world or moving a server.
*Try it:* Open your servers → `/dashboard/games`
*Image:* `files-download.webp` (three items selected, "Download .tar.gz")

### 5. A Mods tab that shows what you have — Game servers — [NEXT UPDATE] (feature/mods-tab-rework)
Your installed mods now sit in one library with version, source and health. Switch mods off and back on
where that is safe for your game, and browse the Mod store for mods that fit your server.
*Try it:* Manage mods → `/dashboard/games`
*Image:* `mods-library.webp` (Installed mods library with health badges and switches)

### 6. No player caps from us — Game servers — [NEXT UPDATE] (feature/unlimited-players)
We never limit players by plan. Each plan shows a recommended player count for smooth play, and the Max
players setting now goes up to the game's own limit.
*Try it:* Check your settings → `/dashboard/games`
*Image:* `unlimited-players.webp` (wizard plan cards marked Unlimited players)

### 7. The server directory, inside your dashboard — Dashboard — [NEXT UPDATE] (feature/portal-directory)
Browse public game servers by game or region, open a server's page to copy its address, save favourites,
and choose which of your own servers to list.
*Try it:* Browse servers → `/dashboard/directory`
*Image:* `directory.webp` (Browse by game grid)

---

## Honesty notes (why the copy says what it says)
- No numbers or performance claims. "Newest release" = the wizard's real per-type default (lib/mcjars/default-version.ts).
- Bedrock: only NEW servers are claimed (existing ones were never affected — their server.properties already used RakNet). "A build we have tested" = the pinned BEDROCK_KNOWN_GOOD_VERSION.
- Player caps: "up to the game's own limit" because some games have an engine cap; we never say "unlimited" for those.
- Directory: "choose which of your own servers to list" only — listing servers hosted elsewhere is a default-OFF source, so it is not claimed.
- Live chat: "the moment they are sent" describes the realtime (SSE) delivery; there is a 4 s poll fallback, so no latency number is quoted.
- Brand voice: no "provider", no OVH, Nxeon speaks as the owner.

## Screenshots (this folder)

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

entries.name: TaskStop
entries.description:
- Stops a running background task by its ID
- Takes a task_id parameter identifying the task to stop
- To stop an agent-team teammate, pass its agent ID ("name@team") or bare teammate name as task_id
- To stop a background agent spawned with a name, pass that name as task_id

That confirms it: 2 unread matches simcopy plus legacy. Now I see why the changelog read never registered — the IntersectionObserver uses a 0.35 area threshold, but the release block is over 2.8x the viewport height, so it can never hit 35% visibility. I should also set thresholds to [0, 0.35] and mark it read if either the ratio hits 0.35 or the visible height covers at least half the viewport. On top of that, I need to make modal images load eagerly, compact the mobile header by hiding the summary, and have the light-mode screenshot wait longer for the dialog role before capturing.

## What's New overhaul: done (not merged, not deployed)

The overhaul and the new draft release are on branch **`feature/whats-new-overhaul`** in worktree `/tank/nxeon-wt-whatsnew`, in two commits: `7967d4b43f` (the overhaul) and `c08b9557ae` (the draft release, its graphics and some fixes). Nothing was written to the prod database (SELECTs only), no email was sent, and nothing was built in /opt/nxeon.

### 1. Audit: what was wrong before
- The admin form could only create. There was no edit, no schedule and no confirm before publishing.
- The admin "preview" was a hand-copied version of the popup and had already drifted from it.
- The `/dashboard/whats-new` page ignored targeting. The popup applied it, so the two disagreed.
- A new signup got every past update one modal at a time.
- No "remind me later", no "Try it" link, and the popup's colours didn't follow the dashboard theme.
- `components/customer/WhatsNew.tsx` was dead code.
- Prod today has 2 rows, both DRAFT.

### 2. What changed
**Database (additive only).** Migration is `prisma/manual-migration-whats-new-overhaul.sql`. It is safe to re-run, and on a scratch database it leaves no difference from the new schema. It adds:
- a short summary, highlight cards and categories for each release;
- a SCHEDULED status;
- audience (all customers / game-server owners / VPS owners) and optional regions;
- an announcement-email switch, off by default;
- read / "remind me later" state per customer;
- a delivery table so the email can only go to each person once.

**Rules (`lib/whats-new/core.ts`).**
- Links must be in-app paths, and images must be our own files with alt text.
- A scheduled release goes live by itself when its time passes.
- **Publish and Schedule are refused while any highlight is marked "ships with the next update".** That marker is only shown to admins; customers never receive it.
- The unread dot counts unread and snoozed releases. The dialog opens by itself only for the newest unread one.
- Releases from before a customer signed up don't count as new for them.

**Customer side.**
- A sparkles button with an unread dot sits in the topbar next to the bell.
- It opens the latest release: a dialog on desktop, a full-screen sheet on phones. Each highlight is a card with an image and a "Try it" link.
- The dialog is accessible: focus moves in and stays in, Esc closes it, it respects reduced motion, and it works in light and dark.
- Closing it counts as read. "Remind me later" snoozes it for 24 hours.
- The changelog page groups releases by day and has filters for the six categories, plus search and "Mark all read".
- Customers only see releases aimed at them. Read state is never written, and the dialog never pops up, while an admin is impersonating.
- This replaces the old popup.

**Admin side (`/admin/announcements`).**
- Create and edit releases, with a highlight editor (reorder, category, live vs next update, image, alt text, link).
- Audience, regions and the email toggle (off by default, with a confirm that names it at publish).
- A live preview drawn with the same components customers see.
- Per release: Preview, Mark all live, Publish now, Schedule, Unpublish, Delete, plus read and emailed counts.
- **Admin-only preview URL: `/dashboard/whats-new/preview/<id>`.** It shows the release inside the real dashboard with the dialog open, and writes no read state.

**Email.** A worker job runs every 5 minutes. It only handles live releases that have the toggle on, and only sends to verified customers the release targets. It uses the product-news preference and includes an unsubscribe link.

**Tests.** tsc is clean. Pure tests in `test/whats-new.test.ts`: 17/17 pass. Database tests in `test/whats-new-db.test.ts` (opt-in, throwaway DB): 8/8 pass. A browser test on the throwaway server confirmed the dialog opens by itself, "Remind me later" snoozes it, and Esc marks it read.

Two failures in `customer-actions-guards` / `admin-destructive-controls` also fail on clean main, so they aren't caused by this branch.

`docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` has a new section on all of this.

### 3. The draft (`prisma/whats-new/2026-10-release.json`; full text in `/root/agent-notes/whats-new/DRAFT.md`)
Status DRAFT, email OFF, audience all customers. As you instructed, it leaves out invoices, status notices, custom offers and the theme animation, plus all internal items.

**"Easier mods, folder downloads and a faster live chat"**
*Seven improvements for game server owners: quicker Minecraft setup, a rebuilt Mods tab, downloads from the Files tab, no player caps from us, a server directory in your dashboard, and a live chat that keeps up with you.*

1. **Minecraft starts on the newest version** [LIVE]: "When you deploy a Vanilla, Paper or Purpur server, the newest Minecraft release is now picked for you, so your server matches what your players run. You can still choose any other version."
2. **Bedrock servers ready to join on the latest version** [LIVE]: "Fixed: a new Bedrock server on the newest version could start without opening its game port. New Bedrock servers now run a build we have tested and open their port straight away."
3. **Live chat that keeps up with you** [NEXT UPDATE]: "Messages arrive the moment they are sent. You can see when our team is typing and when your message has been seen, paste or drag in screenshots, and chat full screen on your phone."
4. **Download files and whole folders** [NEXT UPDATE]: "Download any file from the Files tab, or tick several files and folders and get them as one .tar.gz archive. Handy for keeping a copy of your world or moving a server."
5. **A Mods tab that shows what you have** [NEXT UPDATE]: "Your installed mods now sit in one library with version, source and health. Switch mods off and back on where that is safe for your game, and browse the Mod store for mods that fit your server."
6. **No player caps from us** [NEXT UPDATE]: "We never limit players by plan. Each plan shows a recommended player count for smooth play, and the Max players setting now goes up to the game's own limit."
7. **The server directory, inside your dashboard** [NEXT UPDATE]: "Browse public game servers by game or region, open a server's page to copy its address, save favourites, and choose which of your own servers to list."

- I checked each item against main and its branch. The two "live" items are on main, and the prod build was made after the newest of them.
- Bedrock copy only claims new servers, because existing ones were never affected.
- Copy on item 6 says "up to the game's own limit" because some games have their own hard cap.
- Copy on item 7 doesn't claim listing servers hosted elsewhere, because that option is off by default.
- No stats, no "provider", no OVH. A test enforces this on the draft file.

**Graphics** (`public/whats-new/2026-10-release/`, 8 WebP files, 349 KB total; every card has one):
- A header image with the logo.
- Framed shots of live chat (06), files multi-select, the Mods installed library, the wizard plan tiles and the directory game grid, all from the other agents' captures, showing placeholder data only.
- A fresh capture of the Minecraft wizard with Vanilla and 26.3 preselected (the version picker sits under Advanced settings).
- A drawn Bedrock illustration with no fake UI.

### Screenshots: `/root/agent-notes/whats-new/`
- `01`–`04`: the draft in the admin preview, dialog and changelog, desktop and mobile, with the owner-only Live / Next-update badges.
- `05`: the editor.
- `06`–`13`: the customer view after publishing, desktop / mobile / light mode / Support filter / topbar after reading. These are simulated in the throwaway database with a copy of the draft marked all-live.
- In `05` the form happens to be open on that simulated copy, which is why every item reads "Live now". The real draft is the row in the list showing "5 ship with next update".

### How you preview and publish after deploy
1. Apply the migration (`psql "$DATABASE_URL" -f prisma/manual-migration-whats-new-overhaul.sql`, or `prisma db push`), then deploy through the promote script.
2. Load the draft: `npx tsx prisma/seed-whats-new.ts prisma/whats-new/2026-10-release.json --allow-prod`. It always creates a DRAFT and refuses the prod database without that flag.
3. Open `/dashboard/whats-new/preview/<id>`. The seed prints the id.
4. Once the five branches are live, press **Mark all live**, then **Publish now** or **Schedule**. Leave the email off unless you want it.

### Things you should know
- **`/root/nxeon-credentials.txt` was overwritten again.** Running `prisma/seed.ts` on the throwaway database overwrote that file with a throwaway login, the same thing that happened on 2026-09-26. The prod database and password weren't touched. I couldn't find a backup copy of the file. I've added a suggested task to stop the seed overwriting that file; I didn't rotate or reset anything.
- **I briefly disturbed my own worktree.** While checking whether the two test failures existed on main, I ran `git stash` and `git checkout main -- .` inside the worktree. I restored it straight away and checked the result: `git status` showed only my own pending edits, which went into commit `c08b9557ae`. The other two entries in the repo's stash list belong to someone else and weren't touched.
- **Cleanup:** the dev server is stopped (killed by its own PID) and the throwaway Postgres (`/tank/wn-pg`, port 55481) is stopped.
- **Worktree `node_modules`:** it's a real copied folder, not a symlink, and was never staged.
